title: GitLab week 7 review - faster, modular, safer
description: Eight questions on efficiency, child pipelines, components, scanners and protections.

questions.prompt: Jobs wait a long time before starting. Which fix is right?

options.text: More runners / capacity - queued time is not a YAML problem

questions.explanation: Read queued time separately from duration.

questions.prompt: Why should deploy jobs be interruptible: false?

options.text: A newer pipeline must not cancel a half-finished deployment

questions.explanation: Auto-cancel redundant pipelines is great for tests, dangerous for deploys.

questions.prompt: What changes when you add strategy: depend to a trigger job?

options.text: The parent's trigger job waits for the child and takes its status
The child gets the parent's artifacts

questions.explanation: Without it the trigger job is green as soon as the child starts.

questions.prompt: When are $[[ inputs.x ]] in a CI/CD component substituted?

options.text: At job runtime in the shell
When the pipeline is created, before any job runs - unknown inputs fail creation
When the runner pulls the image

questions.explanation: Inputs shape structure; variables carry runtime values.

questions.prompt: What does a scanner template add by default, and what is its effect on merging?

options.text: Scan jobs in the test stage that report findings with allow_failure: true - they do not block by themselves

questions.explanation: Use approval and scan-execution policies to make them rules.

questions.prompt: Which mechanism guarantees a scanner runs even if someone deletes the include line?

options.text: A comment asking them not to
A scan execution policy at group level

questions.explanation: Policies are enforced outside the project's YAML.

questions.prompt: A feature-branch job echoes a protected variable. What does it print?

options.text: An empty string - protected variables reach only protected refs

questions.explanation: Protection decides exposure; masking only filters logs.

questions.prompt: Why is a CODEOWNERS rule on .gitlab-ci.yml a security control?

options.text: Changes to the pipeline itself need the platform team's approval - the pipeline runs with the project's secrets

questions.explanation: The pipeline is production code; guard who changes it.
